name: Bath
description: Town in Somerset, Stonehenge Tribunal, on the River Avon, famed since ancient times for healing hot springs founded by King Bladud; now dominated by the Church and its priory.

name: Bear Island
description: Peninsula off Anatolia on the southern shore of the Sea of Marmara in the Thebes Tribunal, visited by Jason and the Argonauts; home to the Gegenees, the Idaian Daktyls and the bound titaness Dindyméné.

name: Cursewood
description: Cursed, haunted forest in remote Pomerania near Novgorod, Rhine Tribunal, where a Tytalus magus vanished over a century ago; it has an Infernal aura.

name: Farne Islands
description: Small archipelago in the Stonehenge Tribunal off Northumberland, with a saint's influence on the inner islands and wilder forces, selkie courts and demons on the outer ones.

name: Inner Farne
description: Island of the Farne Islands once home to a saint who drove demons from it to the outer islands.

name: Crumstone Rock
description: Outer islet of the Farne Islands whose mysterious inhabitant is one of the archipelago's mysteries.

name: Megstone
description: Isolated islet of the Farne Islands associated with the Demons of Megstone.

name: Poisoned Battlefield
description: Arsenic-poisoned site in the Mendip Hills, Stonehenge Tribunal, once haunted by an archnecromancer, druid ghosts and dead Roman miners.

name: Mendip Hills
description: Hills in Somerset where Roman miners worked and where the Poisoned Battlefield lies.

name: Wookey Hole
description: Cave site near the Poisoned Battlefield associated with the Witch of Wookey Hole.

name: Buckland Saint Mary
description: Somerset place described as where the faeries fear to go.

name: Purgatory of Saint Patrick
description: Irish pilgrimage site in the Hibernian Tribunal: a cave under an island in a lake, said to be a gate to Purgatory opened by Saint Patrick, leading onward to the Earthly Paradise or Hell.

name: Saint's Island
description: Island on the lake whose cave is the entrance to the Purgatory of Saint Patrick.

name: Patrick's Island
description: Island associated with the Purgatory of Saint Patrick, home of the Canons of Patrick's Island.

name: Purgatory
description: Otherworld of purgation reachable through Saint Patrick's cave, containing sites such as the Field of Chains, the Wheel of Fire and the Bridge to Paradise.

name: Earthly Paradise
description: Paradise that survivors of the Purgatory of Saint Patrick may enter.

name: Hell
description: Infernal realm to which those trapped in Purgatory may be consigned; its Mouth is one of Purgatory's features.

name: Fallen Temple of Mercury
description: Large ruined Roman temple complex built by Augustus, the size of a small town, lying in a Magic regio whose entrance can be in any former Roman territory; a source of Mercurian rituals.

name: Faerie Toy Market on Devil's Lane
description: Faerie regio with entrances in many cities selling magical toys made by hidden elves, containing a Merinita covenant.

name: Devil's Lane
description: Street of the faerie toy market regio.

name: Devil's Lane Covenant
description: Merinita covenant built within the faerie toy fair regio; not secret, and known to the Redcaps.

name: Realm of the Truffles
description: Regio that is a source of truffles, located near Dijon, in Périgord, Istria or the Bohemian Forest, ruled by the Truffle Matron.

name: Wolf's Court
description: Cairn in a remote wolf-haunted forest, nominally in the Provençal Tribunal, where the wronged ask the wolves for justice at the rising of the full moon.

name: Fane of Vengeance
description: Site within the Wolf's Court chapter.

name: Majarida Mountains
description: Mountains whose wolves are associated with the Wolf's Court.

name: Sea of Marmara
description: Sea on the north coast of Anatolia on whose southern shore lies Bear Island.

name: Anatolia
description: Region whose coast Bear Island lies off.

name: Pomerania
description: Region of remote forests near Novgorod where the Cursewood lies.

name: Somerset
description: English county containing Bath, the Mendip Hills and many local legends.

name: Temple of Apollo in London
description: Lost temple in New Troy (London), founded by the Hyperboreans, where Bladud fell to his death and is buried.

name: New Troy
description: Ancient name for London.

name: University at Stamford
description: University of necromancers founded by Bladud at Stamford and later suppressed by the Church for heresy.

name: Stamford
description: Town with odd traditions, site of Bladud's university and possibly a second fermenter.

name: Kaerbadon
description: Capital of King Bladud, suggested as the site of the Battle of Mons Badonicus.

name: Glastonbury
description: Area near Bath liked by faeries, who conflate it with Avalon; home of monks opposed to Joscelin.

name: Glastonbury Tor
description: Pre-Roman site the Bishop of Wells can allow magi to examine.

name: Avalon
description: Legendary place faeries conflate with Glastonbury.

name: Isle of Man
description: Island Christianized by Saint Patrick where a faerie in Mannanan's form prevents a stable covenant.

name: Bath Abbey
description: The Norman cathedral priory of Bath, still called Bath Abbey by locals, operated by around 40 monks and running the baths.

name: Bishop's Quarter
description: South-east corner of Bath containing the palace, priory and baths.

name: Hospital of Saint John the Baptist
description: Hospital inside Bath for the infirm poor, whose inmates in blue robes are called the Blue Alms.

name: Wells
description: City of Joscelin's birth, seat of the Bishop of Somerset, where he plans to build a great cathedral.

name: River Avon
description: River on which Bath lies.

name: Sijilmasa
description: Saharan caravan town with wonderful healing baths built by a mysterious benefactor.

name: Baden
description: Town on the border of the Greater Alps and Rhine Tribunals containing a Mercere House.

name: Hot Baths
description: One of the three main public baths of Bath.

name: Cross Baths
description: Baths of Bath used by lepers.

name: Baths of Alaron
description: One of Bath's three main baths, named for Bladud's consort or for Latin inscriptions; renamed the King's Bath in 1225.

name: Baths of Bladud
description: Possible fourth, hidden set of baths deep underground lit by Bladud's ceaseless fires, whose waters suppress the Gift's social effects.

name: Keynsham
description: Village northeast of Bath named for Saint Keyne.

name: Abbey of Saint Keyne
description: Abbey at Keynsham whose monks guard Saint Keyne's Well.

name: Saint Keyne's Well
description: Miraculous well; whichever spouse drinks first gains the upper hand in marriage.

name: Mount Saint Michael
description: Place where Saint Keyne's brother lived and she left a magical chair.

name: Somerset Moors and Levels
description: Wild marshy areas west of Bath where Saint Keyne turned snakes and dragons to stone.

name: Stanton Drew
description: Megalithic rings west of Bath formed from a wedding party turned to stone; their tears hold Terram vis.

name: Pagan's Hill
description: Hill above Chewstoke, site of an Imperial Mercurian temple with a Magic aura of 2.

name: Chewstoke
description: Village west of Stanton Drew below Pagan's Hill.

name: Ilchester
description: County town under strong Dominion where the boy Roger Bacon lives.

name: Ilchester Priory
description: Priory from which the property of Roger Bacon's family is held.

name: Temple of Jupiter Ammon
description: Lost temple in Cyrene in the Libyan desert, source of true Sal Ammoniac.

name: Mount Etna
description: Volcano that throws out a salt similar to Sal Ammoniac; also a variant location for Purgatory.

name: Constantinople
description: City whose Latin conquest affected Bear Island; the relics of the Magi's gifts were kept there until 1204.

name: Colchis
description: Distant land on the Black Sea where the Golden Fleece waited.

name: Artakia
description: The only inhabited town on Bear Island, with a cathedral of St. Tryphaena and a Dominion aura of 2.

name: Kyzikos
description: Ruined ancient city on Bear Island, once minting gold staters, devastated by earthquakes.

name: Fair Haven
description: Artakia's harbor, the island's sole commercial port, site of Jason's shrine to Athena.

name: City Harbor
description: Kyzikos' harbor, now unused, where the Altar of Apollo of Landings stands.

name: Chytus Harbor
description: Man-made harbor on Bear Island's eastern tip where Herakles fought the Gegenees; Faerie aura 3, strewn with vis-bearing boulders.

name: Mount Dindymon
description: Double-peaked tallest mountain of Bear Island, beneath which the titaness Dindyméné is bound.

name: Mount Klapsi
description: Western mountain of Bear Island, wooded wilderness with boars, bears and lions.

name: Bear Mountain
description: Eastern mountain of Bear Island's range.

name: The Isthmus
description: Low swampy isthmus joining Bear Island to the mainland.

name: Cathedral of St. Tryphaena
description: Large ugly cathedral in Artakia holding St. Tryphaena's relics; Dominion aura 5.

name: Shrine of Jasonian Athena
description: Stone shrine built by Jason at Fair Haven; Faerie aura 1.

name: Altar of Apollo of Landings
description: Shrine built by Jason at City Harbor; Faerie aura 1 and terminus of the Jasonian Way.

name: Spring of Artakia
description: Spring northwest of Artakia with a Magic aura 2 yielding Aquam vis.

name: Leimonian Plain
description: Grassy plain between Kyzikos and the Thracian Harbor, holding King Kyzikos' tumulus with an Infernal aura 4.

name: Thracian Harbor
description: Bear Island harbor with a perpetual inward wind; Magic aura 2.

name: Temenos of Dindyméné
description: Sacred grove between the peaks of Mount Dindymon with Magic and Faerie auras 3, doorway to a Magic and a Faerie regio.

name: Jasonian Way
description: Faerie regio path (aura 7) from the Altar of Apollo of Landings to Mount Dindymon's summit.

name: Faerie Regio of Dindyméné
description: Faerie regio entered from the temenos on Mount Dindymon.

name: Magic Regio of Dindyméné
description: Magic regio entered from the temenos on Mount Dindymon.

name: Isle of the Sleeping Fomóir
description: Alternative version of Bear Island relocated west of Ireland in the Hibernian Tribunal and tied to St. Brendan's voyage.

name: Isle of the Blessed
description: Fabled isle west of Ireland sought by Brendan the Navigator.

name: Troad
description: Area in which Bear Island sits.

name: Hallstadt
description: Salt mines in the Greater Alps Tribunal haunted by faeries.

name: Thebes Tribunal
description: Tribunal containing Bear Island.

name: Stonehenge Tribunal
description: Tribunal containing Bath, the Farne Islands and the Poisoned Battlefield.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal containing the Cursewood; a Truffle Matron location option.

name: Hibernian Tribunal
description: Tribunal containing the Purgatory of Saint Patrick.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Tribunal option for the Truffle Matron and Cursewood variant.

name: Transylvanian Tribunal
description: Tribunal option for the Truffle Matron.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Nominal Tribunal of the Wolf's Court.

name: Greater Alps Tribunal
description: Tribunal bordering the Rhine, home of the Hallstadt faeries.

name: House Bonisagus
description: Roaming magi of this House catalog fantastic sites.

name: House Mercere
description: House of the Redcaps, which catalogs sites and controls properties including baths.

name: House Tytalus
description: House whose magus vanished in the Cursewood; many Tytali suffer cthonic leprosy and seek Bladud's cure.

name: House Merinita
description: House whose covenant lies in the faerie toy fair.

name: House Jerbiton
description: House whose social societies may meet at baths.

name: House Tremere
description: House whose vexillations may hold planning meetings at thermal baths.

name: House Criamon
description: House whose magi hold meditation circles; a Criamon seeks a new Bonisagus.

name: House Flambeau
description: House of a magus seeking Mithraic initiation on Bear Island.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of magi that visits, catalogs and appropriates supernatural sites of Mythic Europe.

name: Seekers
description: Group interested in lost ancient magic, believing Britain was an Atlantean penal colony.

name: Legion of Mithras
description: Popular Hermetic Mystery Cult whose Initiation Scripts send initiates to heroic sites.

name: Cult of Mercury
description: Roman cult, an antecedent of the Order whose rituals Bonisagus drew on.

name: Luperci
description: Brotherhood tied to the Lupercalia, presented as a Hermetic Mystery Cult.

name: Wolf Brothers
description: Group connected to the Wolf's Court.

name: Doliónes
description: Original Greek inhabitants of Bear Island, ruled by King Kyzikos.

name: Argonauts
description: Jason's 54 companions aboard the Argo.

name: Hyperboreans
description: Ancient people who founded the Temple of Apollo in London.

name: Atlanteans
description: Ancient people believed by Seekers to have used Britain as a penal colony.

name: Canons of Patrick's Island
description: Religious community at the Purgatory of Saint Patrick.

name: Market Guild
description: Council of merchants of the faerie toy market.

name: The Rat Pack
description: Group in the alleyways of the faerie toy market.

name: Somerset hedge magicians' cult
description: Defunct Mystery cult among Somerset hedge magicians descended from Bladud's university, which Anne could revive.

name: Latin conquerors
description: Victors of the siege of Constantinople who weakly rule Bear Island.

name: Nicaea Empire
description: Byzantine successor state pushing north, expected to reclaim Bear Island.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Empire to which Bear Island formerly belonged.

name: Bladud
description: Legendary Celtic prince and cthonic wizard-king who founded Bath and its hot springs, founded a university at Stamford, and died when his enchanted wings failed over the Temple of Apollo.

name: Trianoma
description: Figure whose followers help catalog sites.

name: Bonisagus
description: Founder who based some Hermetic theory on Mercurian rituals.

name: Leir
description: Son of Bladud.

name: Mannanan Mac Leir
description: Magician-king, arguably Bladud's grandson, fought by Saint Patrick on the Isle of Man.

name: Saint Patrick
description: Saint who opened a gate to Purgatory and Christianized the Isle of Man.

name: Alaron
description: Bladud's consort, after whom Geoffrey of Monmouth says the baths were named.

name: Geoffrey of Monmouth
description: Author of the History of the Kings of Britain recording Bath's foundation.

name: Sulis
description: Local goddess of Bath's springs identified by Romans with Minerva.

name: Minerva
description: Goddess to whom Bladud dedicated the springs.

name: Claudius
description: Emperor who ordered Bath's buildings rebuilt.

name: Alfred the Great
description: King who redesigned Bath as a borough.

name: Saint Alphege
description: Under whom Bath Abbey adopted the Benedictine Rule.

name: William II
description: King who sold Bath to John of Tours in 1088.

name: John of Tours
description: Physician and Bishop of Somerset who moved his seat to Bath and built its priory.

name: Joscelin of Wells
description: Bishop of Bath since 1206 who wishes to move his seat to Wells and build a cathedral; a potential ally of magi.

name: King John
description: King who built the king's house in Bath.

name: Henry III
description: John's son, the young king who uses the king's house in Bath.

name: William Brewer
description: Lord of the Exchequer and multi-county sheriff, loathed but influential; seeks his secret enemies.

name: Weyland the Smith
description: Magician-king who made magic items and flew.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary king whose victory at Mons Badonicus faeries enact near Bath.

name: Saint Keyne
description: Pious virgin saint whose well and prayers produce miracles near Keynsham.

name: King Melchior
description: One of the three Magi, possibly linked to Sal Almelke.

name: Roger Bacon
description: Eight-year-old boy near Ilchester foreseen as a new Bonisagus.

name: Jason
description: Greek hero who visited Bear Island with the Argonauts.

name: Herakles
description: Argonaut who defended the Argo against the Gegenees.

name: Argos
description: Shipwright who built the Argo and carved the statue of Dindyméné.

name: King Kyzikos
description: Ruler of Bear Island killed by Jason; buried in a tumulus on the Leimonian Plain.

name: Kleité
description: King Kyzikos' wife who hanged herself on his tumulus.

name: Zeus
description: God who bound Dindyméné beneath Mount Dindymon.

name: Alexander the Great
description: Conqueror of Bear Island who built two bridges to the mainland.

name: St. Tryphaena
description: First-century martyr of Kyzikos, patron saint of Bear Island.

name: Thales of Miletus
description: Greek sage whose ghost haunts Kyzikos.

name: Brendan the Navigator
description: Irish monk whose voyage is tied to the Isle of the Sleeping Fomóir.

name: Apollonios Rhodios
description: Author of the Argonautika.

name: Athena
description: Goddess honored by Jason's shrine at Fair Haven.

name: Apollo of Landings
description: Aspect of Apollo revered by sailors.

name: Mercury
description: Roman god whose temple and rituals are a Hermetic resource.

name: Augustus
description: Builder of the Temple of Mercury.

name: Regulus
description: Tytalus magus who vanished in the Cursewood.

name: Julia of House Merinita
description: Merinita maga of the Devil's Lane Covenant.

name: Bartholomew of House Merinita
description: Merinita magus of the Devil's Lane Covenant.

name: Walter the Book Merchant
description: Merchant of the faerie toy market.

name: Brother Bressal
description: Figure in the Purgatory chapter.

name: Anne
aliases: Anne, a Lady Not Noble But Suitable
description: Forgotten God of Britain's waters in human form serving at Bath's priory; Magic Might 30 (Aquam).

name: Minerva Sulis
description: Sleeping Romano-Celtic goddess of Bath; Faerie Might 25; grants requested vengeance via curse tablets.

name: Xaphan
description: Demon, stoker of Hell's fires and lord of arsonists.

name: Balneator
description: Merry Devil lord encouraging conspiracy and fornication in the baths; Infernal Might 25.

name: Merry Devil
description: Demon encouraging group hedonism.

name: Averna's Hogs
description: Creatures of the Poisoned Battlefield chapter.

name: Gegenees
description: Savage six-armed giants of Bear Island.

name: Idaian Daktyls
description: Ten mystical metal-worker and healer servants of Dindyméné.

name: Dindyméné
description: Titaness mother-goddess bound beneath Mount Dindymon.

name: Halcyon
description: Mythical Greek bird that told the Argonauts how to escape.

name: Fugitive Stone
description: Roaming mooring stone, Magic Might 10, chained in Artakia, longing for Jason.

name: Fomóir
description: Magic giant roused at the summit of the Isle of the Sleeping Fomóir.

name: Tuatha Dé Danann
description: Faeries enslaved to the Fomóir.

name: Guardian dog of Pagan's Hill
description: Spirit in the form of a huge dog guarding the Mercurian temple.

name: Stone snakes
description: Petrified snakes containing vis.

name: Stanton Drew stone people
description: Dancers turned to stone who weep Terram vis.

name: Penitent Ghosts
description: Disfigured ghosts of Bath bath thieves.

name: Hallstadt faeries
description: Salt-mine faeries demanding salt hearts.

name: Balls of Bladud
description: Local will-o-the-wisps.

name: Selkies
description: Seal-folk of the Farne Islands.

name: Puffin Joker
description: Magical puffin causing laughter.

name: Echeneis, the Remora
description: Fish of the Farne Islands.

name: Eider Duck of Virtue
description: Magical seabird of the Farnes.

name: Grey Seal
description: Seal of the Farnes.

description: Storm spirit of the Farnes.

name: Demons of Futility
description: Demons of the Farnes.

name: Demons of Megstone
description: Demons of the Farnes.

description: Magical chair on Mount Saint Michael.
